steps.tx: **IgA nephropathy** pathogenesis involves a **multi-hit hypothesis** mechanism: hit **1** is elevated circulating galactose-deficient IgA1, termed **Gd-IgA1**; hit **2** is autoantibody formation against hinge glycans; hit **3** forms circulating immune complexes; and hit **4** drives mesangial deposition and inflammation. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

steps.tx: Clinical presentation features recurrent episodes of macroscopic hematuria coinciding within **24** to **48** hours of upper respiratory or gastrointestinal infections, known as **synpharyngitic hematuria**, contrasting with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis which occurs after a latent interval of **1** to **3** weeks. Systematic diagnostic evaluation and careful monitoring remain vital for preserving optimal clinical outcomes in these patients.

left.title: IgA Nephropathy
points: Hematuria timing: Synpharyngitic within 24 to 48 hours
Latent interval: Zero to minimal latency
Serum complement: Normal serum C3 and C4
Recurrence: Frequent recurrent gross hematuria episodes

right.title: Poststreptococcal GN
points: Latent interval: 1 to 3 weeks after pharyngitis
Serum complement: Transiently depressed serum C3

steps.tx: Diagnostic renal biopsy reveals prominent dominant or co-dominant granular **mesangial IgA** and **C3** deposition on **immunofluorescence**. Examination demonstrates corresponding mesangial matrix expansion and hypercellularity on light and electron microscopy. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring. Careful ongoing monitoring ensures optimal patient outcomes and prevents secondary complications.

steps.tx: The revised **Oxford classification**, or **MEST-C score**, predicts renal prognosis using five distinct histological variables: **Mesangial hypercellularity** (M0/M1), Endocapillary hypercellularity (E0/E1), Segmental sclerosis (S0/S1), Tubular atrophy (T0/T1/T2), and **Crescents** (C0/C1/C2). Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring. Careful ongoing monitoring ensures optimal patient outcomes and prevents secondary complications.

steps.tx: Optimized supportive care provides the therapeutic foundation. Maximally tolerated **RAAS inhibition**, intensive blood pressure control targeting systolic below **120** mmHg, and **SGLT2 inhibitors**, supported by the **DAPA-CKD** and EMPA-KIDNEY trials, slow chronic progression. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

steps.tx: Targeted mucosal immunosuppression represents a major advance. Targeted-release oral **budesonide**, marketed as **Nefecon**, administered at **16** mg daily for **9** months in the **NefIgArd trial**, delivered corticosteroid locally to mucosal **Peyer patches**, significantly reducing proteinuria and preserving eGFR. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

steps.tx: The randomized **PROTECT trial** evaluated **sparsentan**, a dual **endothelin A** and angiotensin II receptor blocker dosed at **400** mg daily. Sparsentan achieved significantly greater sustained reduction in proteinuria compared with active control irbesartan in high-risk IgA nephropathy. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring.

left.title: Dual Receptor Blockade
points: Targets: Endothelin ETA and angiotensin AT1 receptors
Hemodynamics: Reduces podocyte stress and intraglomerular pressure
Trial data: Superior proteinuria decline in PROTECT trial

right.title: Standard ARB Monotherapy
points: Target: Isolated angiotensin AT1 receptor blockade

steps.tx: **IgA vasculitis**, historically designated as **Henoch-Schonlein purpura**, combines identical mesangial IgA nephropathy histology with systemic leukocytoclastic vasculitis. Patients present with non-thrombocytopenic **palpable purpura** over lower extremities, arthralgias, and abdominal pain. Thorough clinical assessment and laboratory correlation remain vital for accurate diagnosis and patient monitoring. Careful ongoing monitoring ensures optimal patient outcomes and prevents secondary complications.
